messages:
maria_acme: I accepted the invite via Okta SSO but when I open project 'acme-web' I get a 403. I can see the org dashboard though. Email: maria@acme.com

sam_support: sorry about that — can you confirm org id + project slug? did you accept via the SSO redirect or the email link? screenshot helps too.

maria_acme: Org: org_9876, project slug: acme-web. Accepted from Okta redirect. When I go to Projects > acme-web it says 'Permission denied (403)'.

sam_support: looping in infra: @jordan_engineer — any idea if SCIM/group mappings changed for org_9876?

jordan_engineer: pulling audit... initial check: SCIM group "acme-projects" appears removed 2026-02-28T15:12:03Z. That would drop project role bindings. Can you confirm your Okta group name?

maria_acme: Our Okta group is named "ACME_Engineers" — we renamed groups last week.

sam_support: that rename would explain it. two paths: re-map the Okta group to the existing project role in our SCIM integration, or assign a project role directly while your IdP mapping is fixed. Which do you prefer?

maria_acme: Prefer fix in Okta but need access now. Is there a quick workaround?

jordan_engineer: quick repro command for support ops (internal):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <support-token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_9876/members?email=maria@acme.com"
```
response shows: `{"email":"maria@acme.com","org_role":"viewer","project_bindings":[]}` — so no project-level role was bound.

sam_support: thanks. @ops_oncall can you add a temporary Project Editor binding to maria@acme.com on acme-web while customer updates their Okta mapping?

ops_oncall: done — assigned Project Editor to maria@acme.com on project acme-web at 1765004325. audit id: audit_8421.

maria_acme: I refreshed and I can access project now, can see settings and pipelines. Thank you!

jordan_engineer: quick postmortem: org setting `inherit_project_roles` had been toggled off during an org settings migration (internal). When that flag is off, org-level role grants do not automatically propagate to projects. Combined with the Okta group rename this produced the symptom where invite accepted but no project bindings existed.

sam_support: we'll follow up with your Okta admin to re-create the SCIM mapping and recommend re-enabling inheritance if desired. Also filing a small UX change: surface when an invite accepted user has no project bindings so it's not confusing.

maria_acme: ack, thanks. Can you email the Okta admin note to admin@acme.com?

sam_support: will do. attaching relevant logs and the audit id. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: AuditLog: role-assignment ops_oncall -> maria@acme.com project:acme-web at 1765004325; SCIM detected group rename ACME_Engineers at 1765004302.

maria_acme: confirmed everything working on my side. thanks for the quick turnaround :pray:
